access_links.label: Preprint: An open-source database of cyberattacks on the maritime transportation system (2024)

description: The Maritime Cyber Attack Database (MCAD) is an open-source collection of cybersecurity incidents that affected ships, ports and other maritime organisations, compiled by researchers led from NHL Stenden University of Applied Sciences (Jeroen Pijpker, Stephen McCombie, Saul Johnson, Rob Loves and Georgios Michail Makrakis) as a cyber threat intelligence tool for the maritime transportation system. Coverage: over 290 incidents from 2001 to 2023 in 54 countries, involving more than 50 vessels as well as port entities, with nation-state and criminal threat actors, drawn from peer-reviewed publications, news reports and government documents; it grows the 46 incidents of the authors' 2020 study. Format and access: an online database described in a 2024 preprint (Preprints.org). Licence and cost: presented as open source and free; no licence was stated on the pages read. Caveats: the NHL Stenden page refused the cloud session, so the record rests on the preprint's abstract; incidents come from public reporting, so unreported attacks are missing. The incident list can set attack types and frequencies for port and vessel control systems in cyber hazard exposure and resilience models of maritime transport. It relates to the ReCAAP piracy reports and the EMSA marine casualty platform in the catalogue.
